metadata.title: 1974 Case 23
metadata.original_presentation: A 72-year-old man was admitted to the hospital because of ulcerations of the leg.

required.content: What is the patient's past medical history?
required.response: Twenty-five years previously he underwent an appendectomy, which was complicated by postoperative thrombophlebitis in the left leg. Ten years before admission ulcerations developed on the left leg, accompanied by pain; he recovered after local treatment. There was a long history of arthritis in both hips. He had ingested alcohol in excess for many years. For several years he had taken an aspirin-phenacetin-caffeine preparation, six tablets daily, for arthritic pains.

teaching_points.content: Chronic use of aspirin-phenacetin-caffeine preparations can lead to analgesic nephropathy.
Excessive alcohol consumption can contribute to liver disease and other systemic complications.

required.content: What were the recent events leading to the current admission?
required.response: Twelve weeks before entry, trauma to the left leg was followed by recurrent ulcerations, which were treated with wet and dry dressings in the surgical clinic. The ulcers enlarged, and he entered the hospital.

teaching_points.content: Recurrent leg ulcerations can be associated with venous insufficiency or other vascular disorders.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic Venous Insufficiency
supporting_evidence: history of postoperative thrombophlebitis in the left leg
recurrent ulcerations on the left leg
enlargement of ulcers
additional_information_needed: venous Doppler ultrasound of the left leg
examination for varicose veins or venous stasis changes

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Peripheral Arterial Disease
supporting_evidence: ulcerations on the leg
history of alcohol use which can be associated with atherosclerosis
refuting_evidence: no mention of claudication or diminished pulses

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Diabetic Ulcer
supporting_evidence: ulcerations on the leg

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
supporting_evidence: ulcerations following trauma
pain associated with ulcerations
refuting_evidence: no mention of systemic diseases like inflammatory bowel disease or rheumatoid arthritis

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Venous Ulcer
supporting_evidence: history of thrombophlebitis
recurrent ulcerations on the left leg
additional_information_needed: examination for signs of venous insufficiency

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination?
required.response: The temperature was 37.7°C, the pulse 92, and the respirations 16. The blood pressure was 165/80 mm Hg. On examination the lungs and heart were normal. There were two ulcerations on the left lower leg, with an impending ulcer on the lateral aspect of the left foot. The skin was dry and flaking, with purplish discoloration. Neurologic examination revealed an intention tremor that affected both hands, the trunk and the head and was markedly reduced after the ingestion of ethanol.

teaching_points.content: Intention tremor can be associated with cerebellar dysfunction and may be alleviated by alcohol in cases of essential tremor.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic Venous Insufficiency
supporting_evidence: history of thrombophlebitis in the left leg
recurrent ulcerations on the left leg
skin was dry and flaking, with purplish discoloration
additional_information_needed: Doppler ultrasound of the leg veins

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Peripheral Arterial Disease
supporting_evidence: ulcerations on the left lower leg
skin was dry and flaking, with purplish discoloration
refuting_evidence: no mention of claudication or diminished pulses

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Alcoholic Neuropathy
supporting_evidence: intention tremor affecting both hands, trunk, and head
tremor markedly reduced after ingestion of ethanol
history of excessive alcohol intake
refuting_evidence: no mention of sensory deficits or motor weakness

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Drug-induced Nephropathy
supporting_evidence: long-term use of aspirin-phenacetin-caffeine preparation
refuting_evidence: no mention of renal function tests or symptoms of renal impairment

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Psoriasis
supporting_evidence: skin was dry and flaking
refuting_evidence: no mention of typical psoriatic plaques

required.content: What were the initial laboratory test results?
required.response: The urine gave a + + + test for protein, and the specific gravity was 1.022; the sediment contained 4 white cells and 25 red cells per high-power field, with occasional hyaline and coarsely granular casts. The hematocrit was 46 per cent; the white-cell count was 5600, with a normal differential count. A stool specimen gave a + test for occult blood. The urea nitrogen was 18 mg, the creatinine 1.2 mg, the glucose 77 mg, the bilirubin 0.3 mg, and the protein 7.3 g (the albumin 4.1 g, and the globulin 3.2 g) per 100 ml.

teaching_points.content: Proteinuria and hematuria can indicate renal pathology, such as glomerulonephritis.

required.content: What imaging studies were performed and what were the findings?
required.response: An electrocardiogram showed changes consistent with an old anteroseptal myocardial infarct. An x-ray film of the chest disclosed minimal enlargement of the heart; the lungs were clear; the diaphragm was scalloped, especially on the left side. A film of the abdomen disclosed marked degenerative changes in both hips. An intravenous pyelographic examination showed prompt bilateral excretion of contrast material; the kidneys appeared normal in size and contour, and the collecting systems and ureters were normal except that a calyx in the left lateral upper pole was ballooned and had a narrowed infundibulum suggestive of localized papillary necrosis; the bladder was trabeculated and emptied incompletely.

teaching_points.content: Localized papillary necrosis can be associated with analgesic nephropathy.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic Venous Insufficiency
supporting_evidence: History of thrombophlebitis in the left leg
Recurrent ulcerations on the left leg
Skin was dry and flaking, with purplish discoloration
additional_information_needed: Venous Doppler ultrasound of the lower extremities

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Peripheral Arterial Disease
supporting_evidence: Ulcerations on the left lower leg
Skin was dry and flaking, with purplish discoloration
refuting_evidence: No mention of diminished pulses or claudication

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Alcoholic Neuropathy
supporting_evidence: Intention tremor affecting both hands, trunk, and head
Tremor reduced after ingestion of ethanol
History of excessive alcohol consumption
additional_information_needed: Neurological examination focusing on peripheral neuropathy

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Renal Papillary Necrosis
supporting_evidence: Urine test showed +++ protein, 25 red cells per high-power field
Intravenous pyelogram showed localized papillary necrosis
History of aspirin-phenacetin-caffeine use

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
supporting_evidence: Stool specimen gave a + test for occult blood
History of aspirin-phenacetin-caffeine use

required.content: What treatments were administered during the first admission?
required.response: Dry and wet dressings to the ulcerated areas were continued, and iron, a multiple-vitamin preparation, acetaminophen, cloxacillin and diphenhydramine hydrochloride were administered. A neurologic consultant made a diagnosis of idiopathic tremor and prescribed propranolol. A Unna boot was applied.

teaching_points.content: Unna boots are used to manage venous stasis ulcers by providing compression and promoting healing.

required.content: What was the management approach during the second admission?
required.response: All medications were withdrawn. Peritoneal dialysis was initiated due to worsening renal function.

teaching_points.content: Peritoneal dialysis is used to manage acute renal failure and remove toxins from the body.

required.content: What was the outcome of the renal biopsy?
required.response: Microscopical examination of the specimen with immunofluorescent technic disclosed marked deposition of IgA in the basement membrane and mesangium.

teaching_points.content: IgA deposition in the kidneys is characteristic of IgA nephropathy, which can lead to renal impairment.

final_diagnosis.name: IgA nephropathy
key_features: IgA deposition in the renal biopsy
supporting_evidence: Marked deposition of IgA in the basement membrane and mesangium
Proteinuria and hematuria in urinalysis
